Beta 1: Search Album Artwork works properly again. Everything in 2.3.0 is included as well. Betas are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Fixed
- **Each result shows how many images it has again.** The count beside every release had stopped appearing, or said NO IMAGES for releases that have plenty, because the archive it came from has been answering slowly or not at all. The counts now come from MusicBrainz and appear about a second after the results. - **The right artwork for the release you picked.** Picking one release, going back and picking another could show the first one's images under the second. - **Honest messages.** A busy MusicBrainz no longer reads as "No releases found", the archive being down no longer reads as "No images", and "No scans" no longer appears while Discogs is still loading. Each source shows its own progress, with TRY AGAIN when it fails. - **Searching stops when you move on.** Closing the panel, going back or starting a new search stops what was still loading, so an old search can no longer replace newer results. - **Discogs no longer waits for the archive.** Both load at the same time. - **The MEDIA filter sees every disc in a set,** so a CD and DVD release appears under DVD too, and HD means the same thing in the list and in the grid. - **Return runs the search** from either field.
### Changed
- **Lighter on your Mac and on MusicBrainz.** The preview loads a 1200 pixel image instead of originals of up to 5000, your own files are shrunk for the grid in the background, and requests to MusicBrainz keep to one a second.

Release candidate 1: Secure Mode for ripping CDs. The betas brought a compact player, rip settings by medium, a new key panel, keys that press like hardware, and smoother motion everywhere. This section collects everything in 2.3.0. Betas and release candidates are offered only to people who turned on Receive beta updates.
### Added
- **Secure Mode for ripping CDs.** Turn on SECURE in the rip settings and CrateDigger reads every track twice, straight from the disc, and compares the two reads sector by sector. Anything that doesn't match, or that the drive flags as an error, is read again until two clean reads agree. When the rip finishes it tells you whether every track was verified, and if a spot never read the same way twice, which track and how far in, so you can clean the disc and rip that track again. It takes about twice as long as a normal rip, so it is off unless you turn it on. If your drive can't report read errors, Secure Mode says so before it starts instead of ripping anything unverified. - **A key for the compact player.** The key panel at the top left now has a Compact Player key, so the slim player is one click away. The expand key beside the cover brings the full console back. - **Reduce Motion is respected.** With Reduce Motion turned on in System Settings, panes and panels stop sliding and fade or switch at once instead, the spinning record and the Rescan arrow hold still, and lists jump to the selection rather than gliding. Lights and fades still glow as usual. - **Pick the medium, then how much of it to keep.** The conversion panel has a new MEDIUM menu (CD, MiniDisc, SACD, DVD-Audio, Blu-ray, Blu-ray Audio, Vinyl, Tape, or Any Source) and three TIER keys: 1:1 writes an uncompressed copy at the medium's own resolution, Lossless compresses it without loss, Lossy makes small files. A CD is ripped at 16-bit/44.1 kHz, an SACD's DSD becomes 24-bit/88.2 kHz, and vinyl and tape captures keep the resolution you recorded them at. The FORMAT and BITRATE rows still choose the codec within a tier (ALAC instead of FLAC, MP3 instead of AAC), and a lit key goes dark once you edit the settings away from it. Starting a CD rip sets the medium to CD. - **Bit depth and FLAC level.** Lossless formats get a DEPTH row (Source, 16 or 24 bit), and FLAC a LEVEL row (Fast, Standard, Max). Every level is lossless; a higher one only takes longer to make a smaller file.
- **A compact player.** Window ▸ Compact Player (⌥⇧⌘M) folds the main window into one slim unit, like a piece of hi-fi: the playing album's cover on the left, the full display on the NOW screen with its LED matrix, and the transport and volume underneath. No sources, browser or inspector. Press the same keys, the small expand key beside the cover, or the green window button to get the whole console back. - **Click the cover to see the artwork.** In the compact player, clicking the cover opens the album's artwork viewer, booklet pages and all. - **Each size remembers its place.** The compact player and the full window each reopen where you left them, and CrateDigger reopens in whichever one you quit in. - **Browser shortcuts bring the console back.** Find (⌘F), Go to Current Song (⌘L) and the display shortcuts (⌘1 to ⌘8) open the full window first, then do what they always do. Commands that act on a selection you can't see from the compact player, such as Convert Selected, Play Next and ratings, are greyed out there, and the arrow keys leave the hidden browser alone.
### Changed
- **A new key panel, top left.** The library keys are now icons in two columns: Dig Crate, Rescan, Add to Crate and Transfer To on the left, and Go to Current Song, Compact Player, Mini Player and Settings on the right. Hover over a key to see its name. The CrateDigger name has a row of its own, so a theme with a wide typeface no longer cuts it short. - **Keys you can press.** The header keys sit in sockets in the panel and go down when you press them, and the transport keys now travel too, instead of only changing shade. - **Go to Current Song moved** from the transport to the key panel. The transport now has three keys either side of Play, so it sits centred with even gaps, the same in the full window and the compact player. - **Smoother motion throughout.** The whole app now moves to one set of timings. Lights come on quickly and fade a little slower, panes and panels move on the same gentle spring, the spinning record speeds up and coasts to a stop, album covers fade in when they load, and the full-screen player and the artwork viewer fade in and out instead of appearing in a flash. - **Clicking a row no longer scrolls it.** Browser columns and the artwork gallery only scroll when the selection is off screen. Go to Current Song still brings the playing track to the middle. - **No bitrate for lossless formats.** ALAC, FLAC, WAV and AIFF have no bitrate to choose, so the BITRATE row now only appears for MP3, AAC and Opus. The display shows the bit depth for lossless output instead, and the size estimate follows each file's own sample rate. - **Columns open on their selection.** When the browser is rebuilt, for example coming back from the compact player or switching views, each column scrolls to its selected row instead of starting at the top.
### Fixed
- **A CD rip can be cancelled.** The cancel key did nothing during a rip, so the only way to stop one was to wait it out. - **Searching felt slower than it should.** Typing in the search field animated the whole browser list on every keystroke; it now updates at once. - **Folding into the compact player.** The app no longer ignores clicks while the window resizes, the player stays pinned to the top of the window instead of drifting up through it, and moving to another display halfway through no longer leaves the window stuck half folded. - **The compact player's status light** sat on top of the display's corner. It now sits above the cover. - **The Rescan arrow spun backwards** for a moment when it stopped. - **Button labels are centred.** Short labels such as RIP sat slightly left of centre. - **Lossless conversions kept their sample rate.** The SAMPLE row had no way to keep the source's rate, so converting a 96 kHz recording to FLAC or ALAC quietly brought it down to 44.1 kHz. It now has a Source setting. - **WAV and AIFF kept 24-bit audio.** They were always written at 16 bits, cutting off the bottom of a 24-bit capture. Bringing 24-bit audio down to 16 is now dithered rather than truncated. - **Opus conversions work.** The Opus encoder only runs at 48 kHz and turned down the 44.1 kHz the panel asked for, so every Opus conversion failed. - **The older Conversion Options sheet** showed a blank bitrate when 96 kbps was picked in the panel, and could not choose Source for the sample rate. - **The window reopens where you left it.** CrateDigger was putting the main window back in the middle of the screen at every launch instead of where you last had it.
